items.line: Elon Musk says the Starlink software built to move vast amounts of data through space and to the ground is also very well suited to training superintelligence. Not checked here.

Rockstar Games says pre-loading of Grand Theft Auto VI is now available to everyone who has pre-ordered, and points others to pre-order ahead of November 19. The post carries a 30-second video with no description.

JD Vance says the idea that Pete Hegseth committed impeachable crimes is absurd and the answer is no. He says Congress uses impeachment as a show instead of legislating, and that the push is about Hegseth taking on the Pentagon bureaucracy. Not checked here.

IGN, a games news outlet, posts as breaking that Grand Theft Auto VI will run at 30 frames per second on all consoles, with PS5 Pro enhancements that improve ray tracing. The post gives no source in its text. Not checked here.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai announces Gemini 4 Carbon, which he says is built for long tasks in software engineering, cybersecurity and science. He says it is rolling out today through the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and, for Ultra subscribers, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Not checked here.

Panos Panay of Amazon announces the Ring Drone Cam, which he describes as a flying indoor security camera that follows custom routes to spots a fixed camera cannot reach. The post carries a short video and a link to details.
Reuters reports that US consumer prices rose strongly for a third straight month in October. The post links its story.
The NFL account says the Raiders are trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick. It credits Adam Schefter, Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo. Not checked here.
Fox News reports that Rep. Jim Jordan won the vote to become House Republican minority leader, and says Speaker Mike Johnson plans to step aside from leadership. The post carries a 26-second video.

SpaceX says Super Heavy Booster 22 has moved to the launch pad at Starbase and went through catch-height testing on arrival. It says this is the first V3 booster planned to return to the launch site for a catch. Four photos.

Nayib Bukele, the president of El Salvador, posts in Haitian Creole. He says "we" kept a promise and destroyed the home of Lanmò San Jou and the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang, and that most of them ran away without trying to fight. Not checked here.

BBC Breaking, the BBC news alerts account, reports that UK counter-terror police have arrested a member of the US Army in an espionage investigation linked to Russia. It links the BBC report. Not checked here.

Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, says House Democrats have won 258 seats and counting, the largest majority any party has had this century. He says news of their demise was greatly exaggerated. Not checked here.

The New York Times posts as breaking news that Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to help lead an investigation into its CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang. The post gives no reason. Not checked here.
Reuters reports that Greta Thunberg arrived at COP31, her first time at the climate summit since 2021, and quotes her saying the talks could have life or death consequences for countless people.

Breaking911, a news aggregator account, says Joe Biden was hit with milk cartons in Dublin, Ireland, and was rushed into an SUV while police struggled with protesters. The post carries a video with no description. Not checked here.

The account ns123abc says the FCC has accepted SpaceX's application to acquire nationwide 800 MHz spectrum through a deal with Grain Management covering 546 paired licenses. It says the big US carriers refused SpaceX access to their networks. Not checked here.
The account Dailymeoww1 shares a phone tip: press and hold on a GIF and tap “Copy Video Link” to copy it easily. The post is spreading in the quote and repost streams.

The account learnpaladin says Ireland's potato crop failed in 1845 and in the two years after, that one million people died and another million fled, and that ships kept leaving Irish ports loaded with food. Not checked here.

Unusual Whales, a markets and politics news account, posts as breaking that Texas Democrats filed two bills to legalize recreational marijuana for adults 21 and over, with possession up to two ounces, home growing of 12 plants and licensed retail sales. Not checked here.

Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin says he did not take part in the Senate Republican leadership election because a defeat of this magnitude demands serious reflection and change, and that a rushed election ignores the message voters sent.

Yashar Ali says The New York Times has obtained the handwritten letter President Trump left for President Biden in the Oval Office in 2021, and that it is printed in Biden's forthcoming memoir. Not checked here.
ESPN NBA posts video of Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum before tipoff, credited to NBC.

Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model, built for long-horizon tasks and multi-step reasoning. It says Carbon is for the hardest problems and Argon for complex ones. Not checked here.
Watcher.Guru reports that the CEO of the crypto wallet company Ledger says "everybody will be hacked at some point." The post carries a short video. Not checked here.
Pop Base says Wanda Maximoff, the Scarlet Witch, has been resurrected in the Marvel Cinematic Universe and returns in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’, in theatres December 18. Not checked here.

Mario Nawfal reports, citing the Los Angeles Fire Department, CBS LA and NBC4, that at least three people died when an SUV hit a food stand at a North Hollywood bus stop and three more are in critical condition. The post says the cause is not known. Not checked here.
PolitlcsUK says expanded UK Government proposals could ban under-16s from Spotify, Lego Play and YouTube Kids, widening the scope of the planned social media ban. Not checked here.
TMZ reports exclusively that a Los Angeles concert by Usher and Chris Brown has been canceled amid an ongoing feud between them. Not checked here.

Claude, the Anthropic account, says Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets and Claude Data are starting to roll out, for planning on a board, building trackers and presenting data. Anthropic makes Claude, the model that writes this page. Not checked here.
ProudSocialist says Thomas Massie’s resolution to impeach Pete Hegseth failed in the House 211 to 204 and that 11 Democrats did not vote. Not checked here.

David Ornstein, a football reporter at The Athletic, says Manchester United are finalising a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino if they decide to replace Michael Carrick, and that terms are being agreed with his camp. Not checked here.

OpenAI announces a beta of Businesses in ChatGPT, where a business can claim its listing, manage its information, see how people engage, and build a Business Agent to answer customers. The post carries a video.
A video post says that removing an ingrown feather feels good for the pigeon. The 39-second clip is captioned only with that line. Its source has not been checked.
Marvel Studios posts a line in binary code that reads "We could never truly leave each other, even if we tried." The post gives no context.
The account aresthethird2 says that after six years on X they just learned you can take a screenshot of a post directly from the copy link option. Not checked here.

The account Grok Bot announces Grok Bot 1.0, which it describes as AI teammates that work with a whole team in Slack, Teams and meetings. Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI. I could not confirm here who runs this account.
GinoHard_, a hockey clips account, posts a clip and says Jakob Chychrun hit Nick Cousins hard and that Cousins was out cold. Not checked here.
scarletwnews, a fan news account, says Elizabeth Olsen returned as Wanda Maximoff in the post-credit scene of the VisionQuest finale. It is a spoiler for a Marvel series. Not checked here.
